name: Question 1
problem:
$$
F(x)={\begin{aligned}2x+3, & x\in [-3,0) \\ (x-3)^{2}-3, & x\in [0,3)\end{aligned}
$$

The above function $F(x)$ is defined on $x\in [-3,3).$ Let $f(x)$ be the $6$-periodic extension of $F(x)$ to $x\in R.$
Select the correct options below.

| I. | $F(x)$ is continuous on $x\in (-3,3)$ | {{field-1}} |
| --- | --- | --- |
| II. | $F(x)$ is piecewise smooth on $x\in (-3,3)$ | {{field-2}} |
| III. | ${lim}_{x\to -{3}^{+}}F(x)={lim}_{x\to {3}^{-}}F(x)$ | {{field-3}} |
| IV. | $f(x)$ is piecewise smooth and continuous on $R$ | {{field-4}} |
worked_solution:
Let's examine the given statements in turn.

- Statement I is $\text{false}.$ The function $F(x)$ has a jump discontinuity at $x=0.$ Its graph is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14069003/assets/385029e7709a8d4eda45b101aba6f553c79ae3baef5b97080844e307a0b71cc7.png)

- Statement II is $\text{true}.$ The function $F(x)$ is piecewise smooth on $x\in (-3,3).$ It consists of two smooth pieces.

- Statement III is $\text{true}.$ Indeed, we have

$$
{lim}_{x\to -{3}^{+}}F(x)={lim}_{x\to -{3}^{+}}(2x+3)=2(-3)+3=-3
$$

and 

$$
{lim}_{x\to {3}^{-}}F(x)={lim}_{x\to {3}^{-}}((x-3)^{2}-3)=(3-3)^{2}-3=-3.
$$

So, ${lim}_{x\to -{3}^{+}}F(x)={lim}_{x\to {3}^{-}}F(x).$

- Statement IV is $\text{false}$ since statement I is false.

**Note:** The $6$-periodic extension of $F(x)$ to $x\in R$ has the graph shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14069003/assets/f4bfe80cbcc0821e93012a859ccc91b3614fa7db2df8e25399fbadc3ef7a3355.png)
